grounding-why: User introduces Batchy.Skill as a skill type/style for calling an agentic skill like a terminal command, with bash-like args, Dotted.Name argument identity, fuzzy/synonym resolution, and --AUTO-style switches; foundational current evidence for the block.

User rejects framing Batchy.Skill as merely layered on Skill.Explicit.Args and clarifies it is mostly the shared calling convention every explicit-args skill should adopt; establishes convention-not-mandate framing.
User corrects the conceptual hierarchy: Batchy.Skill is the skill style and Skill.Explicit.Args is a component; named flags are preferred but clear natural prompts still work.
User refines Batchy.Skill from invocation style to a skill framework interpreting skills as CLI-style calls, and splits -h behavior into its own Batchy.Skill.Help block.

User generalizes subcommands: a subcommand is a named subpart of a skill, optionally activated by an argument action, with files and sections treated as loadable skill parts rather than a special folder structure.

User accepts subcommand collapse into Skill.Arg action, states files and sections are implicit subcommands/modules, and asks to name the generalized concept; evidence for the current modules/action line in Batchy.Skill.

User gives green light to rename agentos-skills-base to agentos-batchy-skills and batchy-skill-design.md to batchy-skill-designer.md; evidence for the current detail reference target in Batchy.Skill meta.
